newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open stronger amid firmer dollar.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open stronger amid firmer dollar.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened firmer in active trade on Thursday, helped primarily by gains in the Canadian dollar overnight, analysts said.

"The improvement in the currency certainly firmed up bill prices, but after the release of the (U.S.) numbers at 8:30 things have kind of just gone dead," said Doug Sannuto, managing director of Canada cash markets with Bank of Montreal.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.09 percent from 3.10 percent at Wednesday's close.

Canadian T-bills began the session stronger in tandem with gains in the Canadian dollar. Canada's dollar opened stronger at C$1.3846 (US$0.7222) on Thursday as investors showed good interest to buy the unit before and after the release of Canadian inflation data.
Statistics Canada said the country's consumer price index less food and energy prices -- so called core CPI -- rose 1.8 percent on the year, in line with expectations.
The report in itself did not have a major impact on T-bill prices but did show Canada's positive inflation fundamentals remain intact, analysts said.

Analysts said Canadian financial markets are now keenly awaiting the release of the Bank of Canada's semi-annual monetary policy report this morning. The report is expected to yield clues about central bank's intentions with regard to domestic interest rates and the currency.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill softened to yield 3.43 percent from 3.42 percent on Wednesday. The one-year T-bill firmed to yield 3.99 percent from 4.0 percent.
The call loan rate traded at 3.15 percent, in the upper half of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
